html:
The people of Etruria, in what is now Tuscany and northern Lazio, who built Italy's first great city civilization before Rome. The map shows them in 500 and 400 BCE.

The Etruscans spoke a language unrelated to Latin or Greek and wrote it in a Greek-based alphabet, which they passed on to the Romans. They lived in independent cities such as Veii, Tarquinia and Caere, loosely joined in a league of twelve. They grew rich on iron from Elba, on trade with Greeks and Carthaginians, and on fine bronze and pottery, and they painted their tombs with banquets and games.

At their height they reached north to the Po valley and south to Campania. Rome itself had Etruscan kings, the Tarquins, until the Romans expelled the last one around 509 BCE. Decline followed. Syracuse beat their fleet at Cumae in 474 BCE, Celts such as the Boii took the north, and Rome captured Veii in 396 BCE. By the 1st century BCE the Etruscans had become Romans. Their cities are on the chart as Etruscan cities.
sum: The people of Etruria, in what is now Tuscany and northern Lazio, who built Italy's first great city civilization before Rome. The map shows them in 500 and 400 BCE.
